$comment: The canonical city state registry (workbook section 20, P2-F; see docs/city/OWNER_CONTINUOUS_CONSTRUCTION_WORKBOOK.md). Every capability (plot) has EXACTLY ONE state here. FLAT means 'no defect on this plot was measured by the four instruments this programme runs' -- it is NOT a certification that the plot is well designed, and the instruments do not yet cover everything section 33 asks for. A plot implicated by a MEASURED defect may not be recorded FLAT: scripts/city-flatness-validator.cjs fails if it is, so the registry cannot be made true by editing it.
unit_of_state: one capability manifest. The composition root is not a plot: it is the platform's wiring, classified in config/capability-modules.json.
precedence: when more than one state applies, the MOST BLOCKING one is recorded: UNSAFE_GAP > MIGRATION_IN_PROGRESS > PARTIALLY_DEGRADED > TEMPORARILY_BRIDGED > FLAT. A plot whose state is more blocking than a bridge it also carries still lists that bridge under `bridges`, so no declaration is lost by the precedence rule.
seal_note: The five states are all that may appear here; the SEAL may contain only FLAT, and section 20 also forbids an undeclared PARTIALLY_DEGRADED and an expired TEMPORARILY_BRIDGED. `node scripts/city-flatness-validator.cjs --seal` fails while any plot is seal-blocking, which is the honest state of a programme mid-migration.

P2-B.exitCondition: kernel -> feature file edges = 0, measured under the ownership map

P2-C.exitCondition: capability-level mutual pairs = 0 and no SCC larger than one capability

P2-D.exitCondition: cross-domain private-state accesses = 0, by explicit owner API, event stream, query API or declared read model

$stages_comment: A stage carries NO typed measurement. It carried three until ledger CC-041 -- '73 edges over 25 pairs', '38 mutual pairs; one SCC holding 20 of 28 nodes', '5 accesses over 3 pairs' -- and all three had gone stale the moment P2-E lowered the real numbers, because a copy of a measurement is a second thing to keep true. The copy is gone: `trackedBy` names the artifact that holds the number and `decidedBy` names the keys that DECIDE the exit condition, so the completion of a phase is resolved live by scripts/bridge-expiry-validator.cjs and scripts/city-flatness-validator.cjs forbids a typed `measured` field here from coming back.
$bridges_comment: EMPTY, and that is a result rather than a default. P2A-BRIDGE-01 lived here until ledger CC-044 retired it: five tests/acceptance/** suites were re-pointed from ./contracts to ./provider-contracts and the one-symbol re-export was deleted, which is the exit condition the bridge's own record declared. The retirement was walked through the replacement lifecycle in config/city-replacement-lifecycle.json -- DECLARED, SHADOW, DUAL_VALIDATED, TRAFFIC_SWITCHED, OLD_FALLBACK, DRAINED, RETIRED -- so the next temporary bridge has a protocol to walk instead of a precedent to copy. The flatness validator refuses a bridge without an exit condition, and the bridge expiry validator refuses a declaration whose literal is no longer in the tree; both were satisfied before this entry was removed.
